title: Dynamic Kernel Advisor benchmark and CI safeguard
creator: Lena Ortiz
description: Purpose: build a complementary benchmark harness ("Dynamic Kernel Advisor" suite) focused on exercising the runtime's kernel-selection heuristics, attention-edge cases, and prefill/decode scheduler interactions. This ticket covers: (1) a stochastic request-sampler that generates a repeatable but diverse corpus covering short/long context, multi-turn chat, heavy KV-cache reuse, and attention-mask edge cases; (2) an attention-optimized kernel profiling mode that captures op-level timings and memory pressure for alternative kernel variants; (3) a prefill+decode scheduler simulator that replays interleaved prefill and decode traffic to surface scheduler regressions; (4) golden baseline creation (deterministic seeds + measured percentiles) and (5) a CI sentinel job and perf gates that detect regressions and automatically create a candidate regression issue with attached artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Harness can replay 10 synthetic workload profiles and produce per-kernel breakdowns (P50/P95/P99) under controlled seeds. 2) Golden baseline artifacts (binary blobs and JSON percentiles) are stored in the 'bench-gold' S3 path and can be referenced by CI. 3) CI sentinel runs on every runtime branch build and fails the pipeline if P95 latency regresses by >8% on the critical workload profile. 4) Regression reports include: diffed percentiles, top-3 offending kernels, and a replayable trace for local investigation.
methodology: We will combine: (A) deterministic trace replay using recorded production traces (sanitized) + synthetic generators for underrepresented corner cases, (B) microbench op-level timers inserted into the kernel dispatch path (opt-in flag to avoid overhead in normal runs), and (C) a scheduler shim that can emulate multi-tenant interleaving and artificially induce memory pressure. Metrics: tokens/sec, latency distribution per request type, kernel-level time, and GC/alloc churn. Each run uses a fixed infra snapshot (instance types, CUDA drivers) to reduce noise.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Determinism vs coverage: seeding gives reproducible runs but can miss rare scheduling interactions.
Instrumentation overhead: fine-grained op timers add overhead; we'll gate them behind feature flags and separate CI lanes.
Infra noise: multi-tenant GPUs introduce variance; will reserve dedicated nodes for golden-run generation.
Storage/cost: keeping many golden artifacts grows S3 storage; retention policy will keep 6 months + monthly archives.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2w): implement stochastic request-sampler and base harness; add a CLI to generate workload manifests. Phase 2 (2w): instrument kernel dispatch and capture per-op timings; create attention-edgecase generators. Phase 3 (1.5w): implement prefill-decode scheduler simulator and replay harness. Phase 4 (1w): produce golden baselines and integrate with CI sentinel job; add automatic regression issue creation. Phase 5 (ongoing): iterate on profiles and tune CI thresholds.
